label: prop:frakD-energy-decomposition
title: Bar-parity energy decomposition: retained ($\cosh$) $\oplus$ emitted ($\sinh$, the $\mathfrak{D}$ channel)
html:
Proposition. Bar-parity energy decomposition: retained (\cosh) \oplus emitted (\sinh, the \mathfrak{D} channel)

Let \sigma be the bar involution (the substrate q \mapsto q^{-1}, an order-2 ring endomorphism) on a field F of characteristic \neq 2. Every energy E \in F splits canonically as

E \;=\; \underbrace{\tfrac{1}{2}(E + \sigma E)}_{\text{retained } (\cosh)}
\;+\; \underbrace{\tfrac{1}{2}(E - \sigma E)}_{\text{emitted } (\sinh)},

with the retained part bar-even (\sigma-fixed) and the emitted part bar-odd (\sigma-negated). The emitted (bar-odd, \sinh) channel is the bar-skew sector P_{\mathrm{skew}}; it vanishes iff E is purely retained.

The bar-skew reinterpretation of E_{\text{unit}}

This is the energy-level form of the complex-volume split \mathfrak{V} = \mathrm{Vol} + i\,\mathrm{CS}: the retained part is the binding-proper (cosh) channel, the emitted part is the radiated \gamma\bar\gamma / bar-skew (sinh) channel. Reading the deuteron law B({}^2\mathrm{H}) = 5g \cdot E_{\text{unit}} through this split makes the "E_{\text{unit}} \in P_{\mathrm{skew}}" reinterpretation precise: if the unit is a bar-odd energy, then it is its own emitted part with zero retained part — a purely decay-channel energy (frakD_is_pure_emitted). This keeps E_{\text{unit}} inside the three calibrations (the bar-skew channel P_{\mathrm{skew}}^{\beta} is the CAL-2 datum), rather than a fourth calibration.

One caveat stands: whether the deuteron binding actually carries this bar-odd character is empirically open (the available data weakly favour a bar-even unit). The proposition formalizes the decomposition itself, which holds regardless; the parity assignment of the physical E_{\text{unit}} is the open input.

The split across the light nuclei

The split has been computed for every light nucleus: the retained energy is E_0 \cdot (\cosh\text{-channel}) and the emitted energy is E_0 \cdot |\sinh\text{-channel}|. The emitted/retained ratio rises from 0.96 at the deuteron — the least saturated, most decay-like light binding, matching its \beta-threshold character — toward 1.00 by {}^6\mathrm{Li}.
